ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1–1.5m. It features a grey-brown body with bold, black-bordered yellow or white rhomboid dorsal blotches and a distinct black facial mask. It belongs to the family Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Mandarin Trinket Snake is best distinguished by its striking dorsal pattern of rhomboid black-bordered yellow or orange blotches set against a dark, velvety-grey ground.
ai.habitat: The Mandarin Trinket Snake inhabits cool, humid montane forests and bamboo thickets in the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mandarin Trinket Snake is primarily crepuscular, often emerging at dawn or dusk to hunt for small rodents within the cool, humid burrows of its mountainous habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Mandarin Trinket Snake is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring, with hatchlings emerging in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Mandarin Trinket Snake occurs in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, typically inhabiting montane forests at elevations of 1,000–2,000m.
